item.title: Correction · Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building: The Helen Diller Family Cancer Research…
item.description: The Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building's June 2009 grand opening came from a UCSF release that could not be read. The opening is now shown as June 2009, approximate, with the sources that could be read, and the exact day is listed as unconfirmed. Source: Wikipedia, UCSF Helen Diller Family Comprehensive Cancer Center (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UCSF_Helen_Diller_Family_Comprehensive_Cancer_Center); SFGate, May 31, 2009 (https://www.sfgate.com/health/article/135-million-UCSF-cancer-research-site-to-open-3229463.php); SFGate, June 2, 2009 (https://www.sfgate.com/entertainment/article/UCSF-s-Diller-Building-better-inside-than-out-3296397.php).

item.title: Correction · Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building: The Helen Diller Family Cancer Research…
item.description: The Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building page now describes its footprint as crowd-mapped OpenStreetMap data, not a survey. Its example of a large Assessor lot is now the lot the building actually stands on, 8711509, which it shares with the Hearst Tower, North and West housing buildings. Source: https://www.openstreetmap.org/way/142845120.

item.title: Correction · Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building: The Helen Diller building page now says…
item.description: The Helen Diller building page now says a 2009 newspaper called it a '$135 million' building without saying what the figure measures. Source: https://www.sfgate.com/health/article/135-million-UCSF-cancer-research-site-to-open-3229463.php.

item.title: Correction · Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building: The size 161,757 sq ft plus 20,000 sq…
item.description: The size 161,757 sq ft plus 20,000 sq ft of vivarium space was not in any readable source; SFGate (May 2009) says nearly 164,000 sq ft and the architect's page gives a conflicting 174,020 with a mislabelled unit, so the record now says about 164,000 and notes the conflict. SFGate says Helen Diller and her husband contributed $35 million but does not call it the largest individual gift, so that phrase was removed from the cost entry and the related timeline entry. The 2006 groundbreaking is now dated by year only (the source gives no month), and the June 2009 opening also cites SFGate. The aerial photo's caption no longer says 'from a departing flight'. Source: SFGate, 2009-05-31 (https://www.sfgate.com/health/article/135-million-UCSF-cancer-research-site-to-open-3229463.php); Rafael Vinoly Architects, Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building (https://www.rvapc.com/works/university-of-california-san-francisco-helen-diller-family-cancer-research-building/); A History of UCSF, 1990-2009 (https://history.library.ucsf.edu/1990.html).

item.title: Added · Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building: SFGate reported in May 2009, ahead of the…
item.description: SFGate reported in May 2009, ahead of the building's grand opening, '$135 million UCSF cancer research site to open,' describing it as the facility's overall cost; the article says Helen Diller and her husband contributed $35 million to build the center. Source: SFGate, 2009-05-31 (https://www.sfgate.com/health/article/135-million-UCSF-cancer-research-site-to-open-3229463.php).

item.title: Complete · Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building: Helen Diller Family Cancer… (~Jun 2009)
item.description: Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building opens in June 2009. Wikipedia says it "opened in June 2009". SFGate said on May 31, 2009, before the event, that it "officially opens Tuesday" (June 2) and that more than 200 researchers had started working in it; SFGate's June 2, 2009 design column calls it "the new Helen Diller Family Cancer Research Building". UCSF's own grand-opening release could not be read, so the day is not confirmed (~Jun 2009). Source: Wikipedia (secondary source; revision 1303846603, citing SFGate); SFGate, 2009-05-31; SFGate (San Francisco Chronicle), John King, 2009-06-02.
item.source: Wikipedia (secondary source; revision 1303846603, citing SFGate); SFGate, 2009-05-31; SFGate (San Francisco Chronicle), John King, 2009-06-02
